title: Error Mitigation
summary: Readout mitigation by inverting the assignment matrix and zero-noise extrapolation by folding gates, and why neither is error correction.
objectives: Correct a measured distribution by inverting the readout assignment matrix
Collect expectation values at noise scales 1, 3, 5 and extrapolate them to zero noise
Explain why mitigation increases the statistical uncertainty of the result
mission: A qubit is measured with the assignment matrix A. Recover the true distribution from p_meas and store in z_readout the mitigated ⟨Z⟩ = P(0) − P(1). Then evaluate noisy_expectation(s) at the noise scales s = 1, 3, 5 (stored in scales and values) and extrapolate to zero noise: store the result in zne, within 0.006 of the exact value cos(0.9).

prediction.question: Each expectation value at scales 1, 3, 5 has shot noise σ. Extrapolating to scale 0 with a straight line, how does the shot noise of the extrapolated value compare with σ?
options: Smaller, because it combines three measurements
The same, because each measurement has noise σ
Larger, because the extrapolation amplifies the noise of the data
prediction.explanation: The fitted value at scale 0 is a weighted sum of the three values with weights of different sign and magnitude. For a least-squares line through scales 1, 3, 5 its variance is σ²(1/3 + 9/8) ≈ 1.46σ², so the standard deviation is about 1.2σ. A quadratic through the three points gives about 2.3σ. Mitigation removes bias and adds variance, which is paid for with more shots.

hints: Readout error maps the true distribution to the measured one: p_meas = A · p_true. To undo it, solve this linear system with np.linalg.solve(A, p_meas), then take P(0) − P(1) of the result.

Folding the circuit G as G G† G keeps the ideal result and triples the noise. noisy_expectation(s) already does this for s = 1, 3, 5. The values fall as the noise grows, so a curve through the points (s, value) can be extended to s = 0.
Fit with np.polyfit(scales, values, 1) for a straight line, or degree 2 for a quadratic (Richardson extrapolation). Read the fit at zero noise with np.polyval(coefficients, 0).

messages.ok: z_readout matches the exact value, and the extrapolated value is within {error} of the exact result, while the unmitigated value at scale 1 is off by {raw_error}.
messages.missing: Store the result in the variable {name}.
messages.readout_raw: z_readout is {actual}, the unmitigated value. Solve A · p_true = p_meas for p_true first.
messages.readout_wrong: z_readout is {actual}, which is not the exact ⟨Z⟩ of the true distribution. Use np.linalg.solve(A, p_meas) and then P(0) − P(1).
messages.wrong_values: values must hold noisy_expectation(s) for the scales {scales}, in this order.
messages.zne_raw: zne is {actual}, the unmitigated value at scale 1. Extrapolate the values to scale 0.
messages.zne_far: zne is {actual}, which is not close enough to the exact value {ideal}. Fit the values against scales and evaluate the fit at 0.
